rulings.challenge_claim: The row files its dod signal under the beloved address vocabulary when the span's only dod-family bytes are the DEFECTIVE 'your loves' object, and three further attributions - verse position, marker location, cross-verse constancy - are imprecise against the bytes.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived object-first, not digit-first. The span's only dod-skeleton bytes are דֹּדֶ֖יךָ (oshb:Song.1.2, tier: byte) and דֹדֶ֨יךָ֙ (oshb:Song.1.4, tier: byte); both skeletonize to the vav-less spelling, which is the DEFECTIVE 'your loves' object (sweep: 4 verses - MT 1:2, MT 1:4, MT 4:10, MT 7:13 [= WEB 7:12]), and I re-checked both address lists: neither MT 1:2 nor MT 1:4 appears in dodi-exact (24 verses) or dod-family (28 verses). So the signal key naming the dodi address vocabulary names an object this span does not carry - the tier-1 dod address-epithet - which is the five-object blend in its field-level form. Verse position confirmed: the span is Song.1.2-Song.1.4, so oshb:Song.1.4 is its THIRD verse, not its second. Marker location confirmed: in מָשְׁכֵ֖נִי אַחֲרֶ֣יךָ (oshb:Song.1.4, tier: byte) the 2ms marker is the final kaf of אַחֲרֶ֣יךָ; the imperative's own suffix is 1cs, so 'imperative-plus-suffix address' mislocates it (the imperative STEM is 2ms at the pointed-byte tier, which is why this is a wording defect rather than a false attribution). Cross-verse constancy confirmed: MT 1:3 carries the span's densest 2ms evidence - שְׁמָנֶ֣יךָ, שְׁמֶ֑ךָ, אֲהֵבֽוּךָ (all tier: byte at oshb:Song.1.3) - and the row splices none of it, while בָּ֔ךְ (oshb:Song.1.4, tier: byte) is 2fs in form and 2ms only on a pausal reading, left undisclosed and genuinely unsettleable with no morphology layer staged. ONE CORRECTION to the challenge's own framing: the row's boundary argument does not lean on the dod key - its stated tier-1 evidence is the 2ms suffix forms - so the blend is a field-contract defect, not a failed voice attribution.
rulings.remedy: Re-key observed_substrate_signals off the dodi address vocabulary to the gendered-form signal class the row actually argues; in boundary_rationale NAME the swept object before any dod word (the defective 'your loves' spelling, sweep: 4 verses); correct 'second verse' to 'third verse'; re-word the MT 1:4 marker as the 2ms suffix on אַחֲרֶ֣יךָ (spliced, tier: byte) rather than on the imperative's suffix; splice at least one 2ms form from oshb:Song.1.3 (tier: byte) into the three-verse continuity claim; disclose בָּ֔ךְ as form-2fs / pausal-2ms and unsettleable. CURE TEST (the test that killed the original): any dod reference in this row must survive a name-the-object check against the dodi-exact (24 verses) and dod-family (28 verses) lists, neither of which contains MT 1:2 or MT 1:4.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row's closing-seam driver is byte-false in position and is voice-identity rather than voice-shift evidence, and no Hebrew at all is quoted from MT 1:6.
rulings.grounds: All three arms re-derived and confirmed. MT 1:7 opens הַגִּ֣ידָה לִּ֗י (oshb:Song.1.7, tier: byte; that opener is 1 verse book-wide), and שֶׁ֤אָהֲבָה֙ נַפְשִׁ֔י (oshb:Song.1.7, tier: byte) stands as the verse's third and fourth tokens - so 'the she-ahavah-nafshi formula opening Song.1.7' is byte-false in position. Substantively: that formula is tier-1 under the moderate policy but it is HER formula at all five of its verses (sweep: 5 verses - MT 1:7, 3:1, 3:2, 3:3, 3:4) and MT 1:5-1:6 is her voice as well, so across MT 1:6|1:7 it marks voice IDENTITY, not a voice shift; it cannot be the closing driver the row makes it. The seam is real and byte-markable as an ADDRESSEE shift the row never quotes: plural אַל תִּרְא֨וּנִי֙ (oshb:Song.1.6, tier: byte) addressing the daughters, against 2ms חֲבֵרֶֽיךָ (oshb:Song.1.7, tier: byte) addressing the man. With no Hebrew spliced from MT 1:6, the row's 'no further addressee change through the end of Song.1.6' rests on the English rendering alone. Tier-4 audit: no modern voice-apparatus heading precedes WEB 1:7, so this seam is not apparatus-derived - the row is clean on that axis. PEER-SIDE FINDING carried forward: the converging primary SUPPORTED this row on precisely the arm that fails, reproducing the byte-false 'formula opening Song.1.7' position - the support item is itself defective.
rulings.remedy: Replace the closing driver: argue MT 1:6|1:7 from the addressee flip, splicing אַל תִּרְא֨וּנִי֙ (oshb:Song.1.6, tier: byte) against חֲבֵרֶֽיךָ (oshb:Song.1.7, tier: byte), each tier-labeled; demote the she-ahavah-nafshi formula to what it is here - a same-voice tier-1 anchor confirming her voice continues - and correct the position claim (the opener is הַגִּ֣ידָה לִּ֗י). CURE TEST (the test that killed the original): the replacement driver must show a marked change ACROSS the seam; a formula attested only in her voice cannot mark a shift out of her voice.

rulings.challenge_claim: The single-verse holding is byte-sound, but the formula's byte position is misstated and the 2ms gender claim is asserted on a morphologically ambiguous form whose in-verse disambiguator is never quoted.
rulings.grounds: Both arms are byte-confirmed, but the severity is understated - the corrected finding is medium, not low. תִרְעֶ֔ה (oshb:Song.1.7, tier: byte) is a prefix-conjugation form whose 2ms and 3fs readings are graphically identical, and no morphology layer is staged, so the row's 'carries second-masculine-singular marking' is not a byte claim at all. The 2ms reading is in fact secure - fixed by חֲבֵרֶֽיךָ (oshb:Song.1.7, tier: byte) in the same verse, with תַּרְבִּ֣יץ (tier: byte) in parallel - so the CONCLUSION survives while its cited evidence does not. That matters more than 'low': this is the cluster's only single-verse holding, it is filed at HIGH confidence, and its entire rejected alternative rests on a masculine-to-feminine gender flip at MT 1:7|1:8 whose masculine side is asserted on the ambiguous form. Position arm confirmed as in the preceding row (the opener is הַגִּ֣ידָה לִּ֗י). Third arm confirmed: 'flips every verb and suffix' is a universal with no adjacent digit and no spliced form, while MT 1:8 in fact carries 6 such markers; the machine universals arm independently flags this sentence. TWO further peer findings: (a) this byte-false formula position appears in TWO rows of this cluster, so it is a CURE CLASS and the correction must be swept, not spot-fixed; (b) the converging primary supported this row asserting the 2ms verb was 'confirmed at byte tier' - a byte confirmation the staged extract cannot yield for this form.
rulings.remedy: Splice חֲבֵרֶֽיךָ (oshb:Song.1.7, tier: byte) as the disambiguator that fixes the 2ms reading, and re-cast תִרְעֶ֔ה as form-ambiguous between 2ms and 3fs with no morphology layer staged; correct the formula's position; give the MT 1:8 flip a digit and at least one spliced 2fs form (6 markers at oshb:Song.1.8). Sweep the position correction across every row of this cluster that repeats it. CURE TEST (the test that killed the original): every gender claim must rest on a form unambiguous at the pointed-byte tier, or be explicitly held.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row argues a four-verse single-addressee unit while leaving the one tier-1 address anchor inside its own span uncited and carrying three of its four verses on the English rendering alone.
rulings.grounds: Confirmed. רַעְיָתִֽי (oshb:Song.1.9, tier: byte) sits INSIDE this row's own span and is the attested tier-1 address anchor of his word for her (sweep: 9 verses - MT 1:9, 1:15, 2:2, 2:10, 2:13, 4:1, 4:7, 5:2, 6:4), re-checked against the inventory; the row neither argues MT 1:9 in prose nor mirrors it into boundary_evidence_refs, and it is the single strongest available warrant for the row's own male-voice reading. The 2fs object suffix on דִּמִּיתִ֖יךְ (oshb:Song.1.9, tier: byte) goes unused with it. Translation-carrying confirmed: no Hebrew is spliced from MT 1:9, MT 1:10 or MT 1:11 - three of the four verses of a four-verse continuity claim. Negation slip confirmed: MT 1:8 opens אִם לֹ֤א (tier: byte), so תֵדְעִי֙ (tier: byte) is neither the unit's opening token nor the bearer of the negation the row's gloss puts inside it. The credit is also correct and I re-audited it: a modern voice-apparatus heading does precede WEB 1:11, and the row declines it on the absence of a gender-marked form - that arm audits clean against apparatus-leaning. PEER-SIDE ADDITION, unraised by either primary: the row's English for MT 1:10 and MT 1:11 stands in straight quotes with a bare numeric ref while carrying verses that have no Hebrew at all, which routes WEB renderings around the curly-quote-plus-inline-web-ref requirement.
rulings.remedy: Add oshb:Song.1.9 to boundary_evidence_refs and splice רַעְיָתִֽי (tier: byte) into boundary_rationale as the span's tier-1 address anchor, with the object named and its digit (sweep: 9 verses); splice at least one 2fs form from oshb:Song.1.10 and from oshb:Song.1.11 (tier: byte) so the four-verse continuity stops being translation-carried; re-cut the gloss of תֵדְעִי֙ so the negation sits where the bytes put it, and stop calling it the opening token. In the same pass repair the quote convention: any WEB rendering carried as evidence takes curly quotes plus an inline web: ref in the SAME field. CURE TEST (the test that killed the original): every verse inside the span must carry at least one spliced tier-labeled form or an explicit hold - MT 1:9, which carries the span's own tier-1 anchor, failed it.

rulings.challenge_claim: A voice-shift seam is asserted with no gender-marked form quoted on either side of it, and two of the book's twelve paseq verses sit inside this three-verse span undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: Arm 1 upheld; arms 2 and 3 do not survive re-derivation. ARM 1 CONFIRMED: the row asserts a shift out of 2fs address into her first-person voice at MT 1:11|1:12 and splices no Hebrew on either side of it. The 2fs form at the seam is נַעֲשֶׂה לָּ֔ךְ (oshb:Song.1.11, tier: byte); MT 1:12's only first-person marker is נִרְדִּ֖י (tier: byte), a gender-UNMARKED 1cs possessive standing beside third-person שֶׁ֤הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ (tier: byte, the melek lexeme - sweep: 5 verses). The row's two spliced quotes sit one and two verses past the seam, so the seam is carried by tier-2 continuity while the moderate policy requires the gender-marked form to be quoted at a voice-shift seam - a real medium defect. ARM 2 REFUTED: the paseq layer is a count-only seg inventory, and the unconditional span-relevant disclosure symmetry runs over the PARASHAH set, not over paseq; this row's span-relevant parashah obligation (the SAMEKH at MT 1:14) IS disclosed, and the marks arm returns clean over the whole cluster. A row that makes no paseq claim owes no paseq disclosure, so there is no symmetry gap here. ARM 3 REFUTED on the bytes: the row NAMES its object ('the dodi-exact form') and 24 verses is that object's correct count, with MT 1:13 and MT 1:14 both on the list; the adjacent two-word run is a separate object (byte tier: 2 verses, MT 1:13 and MT 1:14; skeleton tier: 4 verses, adding MT 2:16 and MT 6:3), but the row attaches NO digit to that run, so there is an invitation to slippage and no actual blend to cure. PEER-SIDE FINDING, unraised by either primary: the row's sole stated evidence for its opening verse is an English string attached to a web: ref that is not that verse's WEB rendering at all - a mis-attributed rendering standing where a splice or a verbatim quote belongs.
rulings.remedy: Splice נַעֲשֶׂה לָּ֔ךְ (oshb:Song.1.11, tier: byte) and נִרְדִּ֖י (oshb:Song.1.12, tier: byte) into the seam argument, tier-labeled, and re-cast the seam honestly: the marked 2fs addressee DROPS and no gender-marked first-person form replaces it, so the shift rests on the disappearance of the marked addressee plus tier-2 continuity, with confidence held accordingly. Replace the English at the opening verse with either that verse's verbatim WEB rendering in curly quotes with its inline web: ref, or a spliced tier-labeled Hebrew quote. Leave the paseq segs and the 24-verse digit untouched - both are already correct. CURE TEST (the test that killed the original): the seam sentence must quote a form from EACH side of MT 1:11|1:12 and must not claim a gender-marked shift the bytes do not carry.

rulings.challenge_claim: The exchange's opening is the cluster's best byte evidence, but its closing seam at MT 2:3|2:4 carries no byte evidence, no forward neighbour ref, and is crossed by an unbroken single-speaker configuration the row never discloses.
rulings.grounds: Confirmed at byte tier. The opening is sound - הִנָּ֤ךְ (oshb:Song.1.15, tier: byte, 2fs) against הִנְּךָ֨ (oshb:Song.1.16, tier: byte, 2ms) is exactly the gender-marked pair the moderate policy asks for. The closing seam is not argued at all: no sentence of the row addresses MT 2:3|2:4, and boundary_evidence_refs carries only a backward neighbour (WEB 1:14), no forward one. The bytes run straight across the cut: 1cs חִמַּ֣דְתִּי and וְיָשַׁ֔בְתִּי with לְחִכִּֽי (oshb:Song.2.3, tier: byte) continue into הֱבִיאַ֨נִי֙ with 3ms וְדִגְל֥וֹ and עָלַ֖י (oshb:Song.2.4, tier: byte) - same speaker configuration, no vocative, no address-vocabulary token, no gender-marked addressee change at the cut. A byte-true single-voice run straddling the row's own seam argues continuity AGAINST the row unless disclosed, and it is undisclosed; under the hybrid granularity rule a cut inside a sustained single-voice run needs a tier-1 marker at the cut, and there is none. Secondary arms hold: the row keeps MT 1:17 inside her turn on the English rendering with no Hebrew spliced, and the token it leans on is the qere in the span's one K/Q-bearing verse (4 K/Q notes book-wide, single-witness) that the row simultaneously declares it makes no K/Q claim about; and אֲנִי֙ חֲבַצֶּ֣לֶת (oshb:Song.2.1, tier: byte) is gender-unmarked and left unattributed inside a unit whose entire warrant is attributed alternation. CONVERGENCE: this is the SAME core defect as the other primary's item on this row, reached from different evidence - see that ruling.
rulings.remedy: (a) BOUNDARY PROPOSAL, explicit boss adoption required - extend the exchange to close at the MT 2:6|2:7 refrain bracket, or re-cut so the single-voice run beginning inside MT 2:3 is not severed. (b) If the cut at MT 2:3|2:4 is retained, disclose the cross-seam single-voice continuity explicitly, add the forward neighbour to boundary_evidence_refs, and lower the confidence. (c) Splice the 1cp forms עַרְשֵׂ֖נוּ (oshb:Song.1.16, tier: byte) and בָּתֵּ֨ינוּ֙ (oshb:Song.1.17, tier: byte) in place of the English for the MT 1:17 arm, and note the qere status of the other 1cp token in that verse. (d) Attribute MT 2:1 at the tier the bytes support, or record it as held. CURE TEST (the test that killed the original): the far boundary must name a tier-1 marker AT the cut, or the row must disclose that none exists and hold its confidence accordingly.

rulings.challenge_claim: The far boundary at Song.2.3|Song.2.4 is argued from mirrored ken/ken parallelism rather than any tier-1 voice-shift marker, and the strongest rejected alternative never engages the live rival of extending through Song.2.4-Song.2.6 to the Song.2.7 adjuration close.
rulings.grounds: SAME DEFECT as the converging item on this row, not a distinct one: both name the unwarranted far boundary at MT 2:3|2:4, and I have upheld it on byte grounds there. This item's DISTINCT and correct contribution is the rejected-alternative gap: the row's only rival is atomizing into single-verse turns, while the live rival - extending through MT 2:4-2:6 to the adjuration bracket that closes the movement - is never engaged, and it is the rival the hybrid granularity rule makes live at this seam. TWO FRAMING CORRECTIONS. First, this item rests its evidentiary weight on the parashah SAMEKH at MT 2:7, called an 'undisclosed cross-seam corroboration signal': that mark is TIER-3 weak, single-witness, never a boundary driver in either direction, and it does not straddle the MT 2:3|2:4 seam - it sits three verses past it and is not in this row's span-relevant disclosure set, which is the SAMEKH at MT 1:14 and IS disclosed (the marks arm returns clean for this row). Using a tier-3 mark as directional evidence toward a later closure is the same tier error the challenge elsewhere polices. The genuine cross-seam device was available at byte tier: the 1cs configuration of oshb:Song.2.3 running into oshb:Song.2.4. Second, the bar on parallelism standing alone as a boundary driver is a distinct rule from the operative-category law this item cites for it. Net: defect real and upheld, grounds substituted, severity unchanged.
rulings.remedy: Covered by the work order on the converging item, plus specifically: strongest_rejected_alternative must engage the extension-to-the-refrain-bracket rival and say from BYTES why it is rejected, or the boundary proposal is adopted instead - one sentence, plus the optional second sentence only for the mandated rival disclosure. CURE TEST (the test that killed the original): the rejected alternative must name the rival the granularity rule makes live at this seam, not only the rival the row can easily refute.
